_about: The reviewed record behind the privacy policy. Everything under 'derived' is read back from the code by privacy/derive.py and compared by tests/test_privacy_policy.py: when the code moves away from this record, review the policy, then update this file and privacy.html together. See README.md.

accounts.google.com.why: Mail and Calendar: the customer signs in at Google and grants read-only access; calendar changes only if the customer presses "Allow changes"

api.stripe.com.why: payments; not in use while access is free

api.telegram.org.why: optional account linking; not configured on the live server (2026-10-31)

api.typesafe.ai.why: the model that decides each browser step (JEV): gets a screenshot of the page and the task text with personal data removed

app.asana.com.why: OAuth discovery, sign-in and token exchange for the optional customer-selected Asana MCP connection

backend.getlumina.pro.why: our server: the app's API and the extension's connection

cdn.jsdelivr.net.why: Browser Python runtime download when a customer explicitly runs a Python delivery; receives client IP and download metadata.

gmail.googleapis.com.why: Mail and Calendar: the chosen labels, message headers and previews, a message when it is opened, changes since the last sync, older-mail search; a message the customer sends and label changes they make (only with the send or organize permission, on their own press or approval)

mail.google.com.why: Mail: the "Open in your mail service" link takes a draft to Gmail's compose screen in the customer's own browser (Lumina sends nothing)

mcp.asana.com.why: customer-selected Asana MCP tools and their authorized arguments

mcp.vercel.com.why: Customer-selected Vercel MCP endpoint and authorized tool calls.

oauth2.googleapis.com.why: Mail and Calendar: exchanging the sign-in code for tokens, renewing them, revoking them when an account is removed

openrouter.ai.why: the experimental browser decider, limited in code to the owner's own account

registry.modelcontextprotocol.io.why: Requested service name during MCP server discovery.

vercel.com.why: Public official documentation URL returned to the customer, no task data fetched by this catalog entry.

www.googleapis.com.why: Mail and Calendar: the calendar list, events and changes, free/busy times and the signed-in address; calendar events the customer creates, cancels or answers (only with the calendar change permission); also the switched-off connectors (Drive)

graph.microsoft.com.why: Mail and Calendar (Outlook, #D8): the chosen folders, message headers and previews, a message when it is opened, changes since the last sync (delta), older-mail search, calendars and events (calendarView); a message the customer sends, folder, category, flag and read changes, and events created, changed, cancelled or answered (only with the matching permission, on their own press or approval)

login.microsoftonline.com.why: Mail and Calendar (Outlook): the customer signs in at Microsoft and grants read-only access; exchanging the sign-in code for tokens and renewing them; send, organize and calendar change permissions only if the customer presses "Allow changes"

recipients_not_visible_in_code.Anthropic: the assistant's model; every model in the server's LiteLLM config is anthropic/* (/opt/openclaw-production/config/litellm.yaml, checked 2026-10-31)
recipients_not_visible_in_code.Vercel: serves getlumina.pro and forwards requests to our server (platform/deploy/vercel)
recipients_not_visible_in_code.server hosting provider: the VPS the service runs on
recipients_not_visible_in_code.Brave Search: receives the assistant's web-search terms (the Brave plugin, a shared key held by the host: lifecycle/cell_config.py setup_search)
recipients_not_visible_in_code.Cloudflare: public DNS 1.1.1.1 used by the assistant's cell to look up website names (lifecycle/cell_config.py RESOLVERS)

policy_must_say: until you ask us to delete

company that runs the endpoint you enter
Allow Lumina to use this tab
optional permission to read all sites

made on our own server by open-source software
sent to our model provider to be read
only if you connect a Google account to Mail and Calendar

What your assistant checked during a task
Removing an account deletes its access tokens and everything Lumina copied from it
only when you press the button yourself or approve a change your assistant prepared
Records of changes made in your connected mail and calendars
at most 50 people a message and 30 messages an hour
It never deletes mail for good
stored encrypted and not shown again
A draft that was sent is removed 30 days

review_log.by: side-panel chat (written by Claude Code for the owner to review; not yet published)
review_log.note: The extension gains the sidePanel permission and one HTTPS call to Lumina's own server (https://backend.getlumina.pro/v1/panel, same host as the device link) for the side chat; it keeps the short-lived pass in memory only, plus one more developer-only setting (panelApi). chat_messages gains a nullable surface column holding only the label 'panel' (no personal data; the typed text already lives in the same table as every chat message). review_log.by: long-term memory (Hindsight), written by Claude Code for the owner to review; not yet published
review_log.note: New table longterm_memories: the plain text of short notes the assistant saved for a customer (preference/fact, one sentence, secrets refused), per account, visible and deletable by the customer, never restored from backups (LIVE in ops/restore.py). Notes are also indexed in a self-hosted Hindsight server (one bank per account, bank id = keyed hash computed on the server, never chosen by the assistant), configured with retain_extraction_mode=chunks and observations off, so it stores each note verbatim, calls no language model on notes and derives no text from them; embeddings and reranking must run locally on the same server (deploy/LONG_TERM_MEMORY.md). No new third party receives notes. Policy updated: short version, collect list, recipients (our memory service, same server), retention row, choices. Feature stays off (long-term-memory.json) until this policy is published and Hindsight is deployed per deploy/LONG_TERM_MEMORY.md.

review_log.by: owner goal: the extension becomes a standalone side chat like other assistants' extensions
review_log.note: New permissions tabs, scripting, contextMenus and an OPTIONAL all-sites permission asked for only inside the side chat. New behaviours the policy now states: the side chat opens on any tab and every open is a new session (a new chat titled "Browser extension", the assistant woken); the extension signs in to /v1/panel/session with its own device token; Lumina can work in a tab of the customer's own Chrome only after they press Allow on it (attached while a task runs, released after, never closed); tab names/addresses are sent only with a message that involves a tab; selected text (4,000) and page text (20,000) are sent only after the customer allows reading pages and are kept with the chat message; saved prompts and panel settings stay on the computer; the popup is gone (controls moved into the side chat). Checked against code: derive.py output, panel.py clean_context, browse/extension tests. Publish the page after merge.

review_log.by: Claude Code, on the owner's instruction to replace Lumina's fixed spending limits with customer-set ones (owner to confirm)
review_log.note: New table spend_limits (migration 0037): account_id, task_microusd, daily_microusd, period_microusd, updated_epoch. review_log.by: Claude Code, completing roadmap Phase 0-1 on the owner's instruction (owner to confirm)
review_log.note: Migrations 0040 to 0042 (692 to 734 columns). 0040: request_slots and cell_slots (which request and which cell is running, with the host it runs on: ids and timestamps only; several customers now run at once). 0041: plan_proposals (a suggested revision of a running plan: the plan JSON, the customer's own change request text, a fixed-vocabulary summary and difference) and plan_settings (the customer's automatic-revision choice). 0042: schedules.prompt (what a scheduled run does: the customer's own words, the same class of content as a message), missed_policy, grace_seconds, approved_until_epoch, conversation_id, and schedule_runs (one row per schedule per day with a fixed-word outcome). All of it is the customer's own content or platform bookkeeping that stays on our server; the assistant request text goes to the same model provider as every chat message. No new recipient, no new retention time, nothing newly sent anywhere; plan_proposals, plan_settings and schedule_runs are restored from backups like plan_revisions and schedules, the slot tables never are. Judged not to need a policy wording change. schema_sha256 and schema_columns updated to match.

review_log.by: Claude Code, roadmap Phase 2-3 on the owner's instruction (NOT YET PUBLISHED: the owner reviews the wording before this branch is merged and deployed)
review_log.note: Migrations 0043 to 0047 (734 to 923 columns). 0043 (Phase 1, not recorded before): conversations.parent_id, plan_phase_runs.conversation_id, spend_marks (bookkeeping, no content). 0044: organizations, organization_members (who belongs with which role: ids only), organization_policies (what an organization decides for its members), accounts.organization_id. 0045: connector_grants (which calendars, folders or repositories a connection may reach, with the names the customer saw), connector_secrets (connected services' tokens, sealed with a key in a root-only file; never exported, never restored), connector_revocations (a receipt of what was stopped: counts), connector_freshness (when a resource was last read: timestamps and counts), refresh bookkeeping on connector_connections, schedules.needs_connection_id and pause_reason. 0046: actions (a change prepared in a connected service: the exact content to be sent, its preview and its outcome; the customer's own content, the same class as a message), action_auto_approvals, handoffs (a question or approval waiting for the customer), workflows, and the synthetic test service's own two tables (hold nothing of a customer's). 0047: account_jobs (the checkpoints and report of an export, a deletion or an offboarding: counts, never content), financial_records (amounts and dates kept after an account is deleted), conversations.deleted_epoch. Nothing in these tables is sent anywhere new: connected services stay off behind the owner switches connectors_linking, connector_writes and synthetic_connector, and self-service export, deletion and offboarding behind account_self_service; the policy stays silent about them until a switch is turned on (README, 'update the policy FIRST'). ONE THING DOES CHANGE WHAT CUSTOMERS ARE TOLD: this release ships the retention sweeper (deploy/agentai-retention.timer, manage.py retention_sweep), which for the first time enforces limits that were only defined: the step-by-step activity record of a task 30 days (and for chats older than 90 days), security records and account email records 180 days. The policy's last retention row was therefore split into three rows with those limits, the summary list gained one line, and the date became 15 November 2026. The rest of the row ('kept until you ask us to delete them') is unchanged and still true. The timer must be installed with this release (PENDING_DEPLOY.md), or the policy promises limits nothing enforces; check_server.py warns when the two disagree.

review_log.by: Claude Code on the owner's instruction of 2026-11-19 ("publish as prepared"), finishing roadmap Phase 4-5
review_log.note: Published the text prepared on 2026-11-16 (platform/privacy/proposed/), dated 19 November 2026. It now describes what was already live or is switched on with it: (1) Mail and Calendar (switch mail_calendar_dashboard, on for every account since 2026-11-16): Google sign-in with read-only scopes (gmail.readonly, calendar.readonly, openid email); the copy kept on our server (headers, previews and labels of the chosen mail until the account is removed; every past event and two years ahead; message text only once opened, kept 90 days after it was last opened, swept by the retention timer; drafts kept in Lumina only); Google named as a recipient of our requests (hosts accounts.google.com, oauth2.googleapis.com, gmail.googleapis.com, www.googleapis.com, and mail.google.com for the compose link opened by the customer's own browser). (2) Files and the document index (switches customer_uploads and customer_knowledge, turned on with this release): uploads up to 10 MB, a per-account index of passages and search vectors made on our own server by a self-hosted model (no new company), pages with no text and possible charts read by Anthropic at Lumina's cost; commitments; what the assistant checked (90 days, swept); memory corrections keep history. file_uploads leaves features_off_so_policy_is_silent_on_them, and check_server.py now fails a feature only while the record says the policy is silent on it. Migrations 0048 to 0050 (923 to 1119 columns): hub_* (the mail and calendar copy), file folders and places, knowledge_* (sources, passages, checks), commitments, organization groups, memory history, mail drafts; every one has a retention row and a deletion step. Retention table gains task_checks 90 and mail_bodies 90 (both swept). Every statement was checked against retention.py, google_hub.py, files.py, hub_sync.py and knowledge_tools.py.

review_log.by: Claude Code, roadmap Phase 6 (calendar changes) on the owner's instruction of 2026-11-20
review_log.note: Migration 0052 (1119 to 1122 columns): connector_link_states.upgrade_connection_id (which of the customer's own connections a sign-in adds a permission to: an id), hub_settings.availability_json (the customer's own working hours, notice, buffer and which calendars count), actions.direct_screen (which screen a change the customer made with their own hand came from: a fixed word). No new kind of personal data, no new recipient, no new retention time. Changing mail and calendars is built behind the owner switch mail_calendar_writes, which is OFF: the published policy's statement that Lumina cannot send, change or delete anything stays true until the owner approves the policy text for changes and turns the switch on. Judged not to need a wording change now.

review_log.by: Claude Code, roadmap Phase 6, approved by the owner on 2026-11-20 ("Approve and publish")
